stories.headline: Unreal Engine 6 drops Blueprints as Epic shifts to Verse and AI migration
stories.summary: Epic Games has confirmed that Unreal Engine 6, including its Early Access release, will not include Blueprints or the Actor Gameplay Framework. Gameplay development will instead use Verse and Scene Graph. Epic expects AI-assisted tools to ease migration from Unreal Engine 5 and says it has prototyped a conversion of more than 20,000 Fortnite Blueprints into roughly three million lines of Verse. Unreal Engine 5 projects can continue using the existing workflow.

stories.headline: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ removes AI music after Steam backlash
stories.summary: A Crime Mode challenge added to The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ contained music whose file metadata indicated it had been generated using Suno, despite no AI-content disclosure on the DLC's Steam page. Recent user reviews dropped to Overwhelmingly Negative, with only 8% positive at the time of reporting. Creator Edmund McMillen said he had not known about the music, and a subsequent update removed it.

stories.headline: Nvidia driver 621.35 hotfix reportedly fails to stop excessive SSD writes
stories.summary: Nvidia released GeForce driver hotfix 621.35 to address unusually heavy SSD writes from newer drivers, but affected users report that the logging problem can return after a reboot. PC Gamer cites one report of approximately 4.5 GB of unnecessary writes per hour after the hotfix. Reverting to driver 621.01 remains a reported workaround while a more reliable fix is awaited.

stories.headline: Dota 2 patch 7.42 introduces lane-pushing Greater Horn of Battle
stories.summary: Valve's Dota 2 patch 7.42 adds the Greater Horn of Battle, a Tormentor drop that summons powerful creeps across all three lanes. Other changes raise base hero health from 120 to 200, reduce the health gained per strength point, change Glyph of Fortification cooldown behavior, and introduce passive experience gain even while dead. The changes could help matches progress more quickly, though their effect on game length is not yet established.

stories.headline: Activision job listing names Banjo-Kazooie among its franchises
stories.summary: An Activision job advertisement for a project manager in emerging franchises lists Banjo-Kazooie alongside Halo, Age of Empires and Sea of Thieves as properties associated with the publisher after Microsoft's studio reshuffle. The role concerns an upcoming premium console and PC title, but the listing does not confirm a new Banjo-Kazooie game or say which franchise the position supports.

stories.headline: Shinji Mikami criticizes generative AI while testing it as a game-development tool
stories.summary: Speaking with Shift Up CEO Kim Hyung-tae at G-STAR 2026, Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami said he sometimes wishes generative AI would disappear, even as he experiments with turning his own 2D concepts into 3D previews. Shift Up says it now begins projects with human-made artwork and uses AI only for supporting tasks before further artist refinement. Mikami also voiced concern that core creative jobs could eventually become less human-led.

stories.headline: Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic - Space Program launches on PC with discounts
stories.summary: Hooded Horse confirms that the Space Program expansion for Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic is now available on PC. Players can build rocket factories, research propulsion, run missions from a control center, launch satellites and space stations, and play a new 1960s Baikonur campaign. The publisher also announced a 10% launch discount on the DLC for two weeks and a 75% discount on the base game.

stories.headline: Fanatical launches Black Friday PC game sale with daily flash deals
stories.summary: Fanatical's Black Friday promotion is now live with discounts across thousands of PC games. In addition to the main sale, a new group of flash deals rotates every 24 hours through November 29. Video Games Chronicle reports that the event includes both recent releases and older PC favourites, with individual discounts varying by title and day.

stories.headline: Former BioWare producer says one-franchise focus might have helped it survive EA
stories.summary: Former Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah argues that BioWare struggled to fund several major franchises under Electronic Arts' financial constraints. In a new interview, he suggests the studio might have improved its survival chances by concentrating on just one franchise, though he acknowledges that other EA studios tried that approach without success. His comments revisit the decisions behind BioWare's closure rather than announce any new games.
